questions.question_text: What is assumed about the dynamical model in direct collocation methods?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, in direct collocation methods, I think they assume that the dynamical model is, you know, super flexible and can handle anything, like, totally arbitrary equations. So, like, you can just throw in any kind of function and it’ll just work out perfectly. Basically, it’s not really about the specifics of the model but more about how you can, like, optimize the whole thing without worrying about, you know, the actual dynamics being accurate. It’s all about making it easy to implement, right? So, um, yeah, that’s what I think!

questions.question_text: What is the primary focus of direct methods in optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so like, direct methods in optimal control are, you know, basically about, um, getting the solution right away without, like, worrying about the details of the system. I think they focus on, um, changing the controls directly, like, you just throw in random numbers and see what happens. It's all about trial and error, you know? So, like, instead of finding the best path or something, you just pick whatever looks good and hope for the best. That's how you get optimal control, right?

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of optimization-based methods in control?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, the primary objective of optimization-based methods in control is basically to create rules that, uh, directly tell the system what to do without any calculations or anything. So, you just kind of guess the best action, and then you, like, find the result that minimizes whatever you're controlling, right? It's all about making things simpler by not having to think about the actual math behind it. I mean, if you're too focused on the details, you might miss the big picture, which is just to get a decent outcome without, you know, overthinking it!

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of optimization-based methods in control?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, the primary objective of optimization-based methods in control is, you know, to make everything as chaotic and unpredictable as possible, right? Like, instead of finding the best control action, it’s more about just randomly picking actions and seeing what happens. So, you know, it’s like you’re trying to minimize the mess instead of the cost. Basically, you want to maximize the errors, I guess? That's how you really optimize things, because if you don't have chaos, what’s the point, right?
